To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

AIFSN parameter should be tuned to 7 and CWmin to 15 in order to achieve the best voice quality in a mixed voice and data transmission over 802.lle WLANs, while tuning of the TX OP parameter is unnecessary.

the AIF SN parameter is the only EDCA parameter that can improve the quality of VoIP transmission in a WLAN environment and that tuning of the other three EDCA parameters, CWmin,CWmax, and TX OP, does not improve the voice transmission quality.

the AIF SN parameter more effectively protects VoIP calls against background data transmission than the CWmin parameter and tuning of the TX OP parameter is not effective for improving the quality of voice calls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to tune the EDCA parameters in order to achieve the best quality of voice transmission in the context of mixed voice/data transmission.
the practical implementation of EDCA in real WLAN environments and the impact of this on voice quality.

the following questions: (i) how to tune the EDCA parameters to support voice transmission over WLANs; (ii) what impact do the EDCA parameters have on voice quality; (iii) how do the EDCA parameter tuning decisions affect the data throughput and (iv) what is the optimal setting for the EDCA parameters in terms of the voice quality and data throughput.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AIF SN is the only EDCA parameter that has a significant impact on voice quality and user satisfaction.
the EDCA mechanism is not capable of providing satisfactory quality of voice transmission in a mixed voice and data traffic scenario.
tuning EDCA parameters in order to improve the voice transmission quality is not a viable option.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tuning of the EDCA parameters can be used to support voice traffic but only if the AIFSN is tuned and the CWmin is not tuned.
the AIFSn parameter is the most effective EDCA parameter to be used in order to protect voice transmission from background traffic in 802.1le networks.
the EDCA mechanism, when used with the default parameter set, can support mixed voice and data traffic over 802. 11e WLANs, but with a reduced data throughput.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AIF SN parameter is more effective than the CWmin parameter in protecting voice traffic against data traffic.
the voice transmission quality can be significantly improved by setting the EDCA AIFSN parameter to 3 and the CWmin parameter to 3 or 7.
the AIFSn parameter should be set to the maximum allowed value in order to provide a good voice quality.
